subject: Infrastructure liability addendum — on-prem / network exclusion (TerraFirma)
messages:
From: Jessica Park <jessica@terrafirma.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02 09:14 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA appendix for on-prem hosting — network carveout

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the model performance looked great. We're now lining up procurement and legal and I need to surface one requirement from our ops team before we can proceed to signature.

TerraFirma will be running the inference stack inside our colo (private deployment) with our networking and cross-connects fully managed by our site ops. Because we control the rack, routers, and DC cross-connects, our infrastructure team is asking for an explicit exclusion in the uptime/latency SLA that covers incidents originating from customer-controlled network/DC components (examples: fiber carrier blips, cross-connect misconfigurations, power PDU failures inside our racks).

We'd like Redwood to:
- Add an appendix that clearly lists what constitutes a customer-controlled network incident.
- Define the notification and verification process (how do we prove a carrier/colo outage versus Redwood infra?).
- Optionally: offer a documented fallback path (e.g., automatic failover to Redwood hosted endpoints for critical routes) and an estimate of what failover would cost.

Attached is a short SOW from our ops team describing the elements they want captured. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept an exclusion like this and what guardrails (monitoring, audit logs, runbook handoff) you'd require?

Jessica
Director, Infrastructure
TerraFirma Labs

Attachment: TerraFirma_SOW_network_responsibility.pdf (1 page)

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Park <jessica@terrafirma.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA appendix for on-prem hosting — network carveout

Jessica — thanks for the clear SOW and context. We can accommodate carveouts for customer-controlled network/DC faults in principle, but we need to tighten the language and operational requirements so the exclusion is unambiguous and doesn't undermine our SLO guarantees for other outages.

High-level thoughts:
- We will draft an addendum that defines a "Customer Network Incident" (CNI) with objective criteria (BGP route withdrawal, provider incident ticket, linked colo incident report, on-site PDU alarms).
- For an incident to qualify as a CNI, we will require timely evidence from the customer's ops team (carrier tickets, traceroutes from our egress, outage window).
- Redwood will maintain its own telemetry (egress reachability tests, probe logs, model process health) and will coordinate a joint post-incident review.
- Regarding fallback: we can offer an opt-in automatic failover to Redwood hosted endpoints for critical production traffic, but this requires pre-configuration (routing policy, auth keys, and acceptance of usage billing on the hosted side). We can provide cost estimates once we know expected baseline traffic and retention.

I'll loop in Vivek (legal/enterprise) and Marcus (solutions) to propose specific contract language and a draft addendum. Can you confirm TerraFirma's tolerable notification window (example: 30 minutes for initial alert, 4 hours for evidence upload) and whether you'll accept scheduled maintenance windows for the colo?

Next steps: I will send a proposed addendum (redwood-addendum-proposal-v1.docx) by EOD for your review.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jessica Park <jessica@terrafirma.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03 08:46 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA appendix for on-prem hosting — network carveout (draft language)

Hi all — attaching a first-pass addendum with suggested definitions and operational controls. Key items in the draft:

1) Definition of Customer Network Incident (CNI): objective signal list (carrier outage bulletin, colo incident ID, aggregate traceroute failures from >=3 Redwood edge probes, customer-supplied provider ticket).
2) Evidence and timing: customer must upload supporting evidence within 4 hours of Redwood's initial incident alert; failure to provide evidence extends evaluation window but does not automatically qualify for exclusion.
3) Verification and triage: Redwood will run egress reachability tests and publish probe logs; both parties agree to a joint triage within 8 hours for critical incidents.
4) Credits and exclusions: Incidents that meet the CNI criteria will be excluded from monthly uptime credit calculations. Incidents where root cause is ambiguous will be investigated under the joint review process; if Redwood's telemetry shows service-side faults, normal credits apply.
5) Fallback and cost: optional automatic failover to Redwood hosted routing is available as an add-on. During failover, traffic will be billed at standard hosted rates; Redwood will provide an estimate based on an agreed baseline TPS.
6) Audit & security controls: customer must provide read-only access to relevant carrier tickets and allow periodic validation tests (synthetic probes) from Redwood's edge. For private key custody (KMS) the addendum specifies that keys remain customer-controlled and Redwood will not have access.

Attachment: redwood-addendum-proposal-v1.docx (redlines included)

Marcus — please review the technical fallback bullets (lines 18–30) and confirm whether the automatic failover workflow and required pre-config (BGP/route failover, credential swap, and auth token refresh cadence) are correct.

Jessica — if this language looks reasonable I can have legal prepare a DocuSign-ready addendum; we will also record an SOW change for billing.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Enterprise Legal (acting)
Redwood Inference

From: Jessica Park <jessica@terrafirma.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03 11:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA appendix for on-prem hosting — network carveout (draft language)

Thanks Vivek / Laura — this is exactly the level of detail we were hoping for. A few quick clarifications before we sign:

- Evidence timeline: 4 hours is acceptable. For long-carrier outages our ops team will share provider ticket IDs and a short summary within that window.
- Joint triage: 8 hours is workable for critical incidents; we request one designated point-of-contact from Redwood for triage calls.
- Fallback costs: can you provide an example estimate for 100 RPS baseline (p95 token consumption ~40 tokens/response) so we can evaluate monthly delta to our costs?
- DocuSign: please send the final addendum via DocuSign and we will route it through procurement.

If you can include the cost example in the hosted-failover appendix and add a line naming the Redwood triage POC, we can get this approved by Friday.

Jess
Jessica Park
Director, Infrastructure
TerraFirma Labs
